extracted.intended_audience: journalism educators, journalism school administrators, and newspaper editors interested in journalism education
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive survey of how introductory undergraduate newswriting and reporting courses are taught at accredited journalism schools, covering course structure, instructor background, pedagogy, assessment, and suggested improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course catalog level
rubrics_metrics.description: At what level is the course listed in the catalog (freshman, sophomore, junior, senior)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey finding: 78% listed 'sophomore', 18% 'junior', 4% 'freshman'; indicates the basic course is primarily designed for second-year students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of offering per academic year
rubrics_metrics.description: How many times the basic course is offered during an academic year (counting multiple sections separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses: 1–2 times (17%), 3–5 times (20%), 6–10 times (38%), >10 times (25%). High-frequency offerings imply accessibility; one institution reported 30 offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic credit allocated
rubrics_metrics.description: Total academic credit the course carries (converted to quarter hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported distributions: 3 qtr hrs (12%), 4 (18%), 4.5 (45%), 5 (7%), 6 (6%), >6 (12%). Guidance notes significance: at many schools this equals ~10% of journalism hours and ~2.5% of overall degree credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course title/labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal title(s) under which the course appears in catalogs (e.g., 'News Writing', 'Reporting').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 29 different titles reported; nearly 80% used 'News Writing' or 'Reporting' or combinations; 'News Writing' most common (22 listings). Title signals scope and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement status for majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the course is required for undergraduate journalism majors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly 80% of respondents reported the course is required for all undergraduate journalism majors—implying curricular centrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor professional journalistic experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of full-time professional journalistic experience instructors have (years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses: none up to 2 years (0%), 2–5 (7%), 5–10 (20%), 10–15 (25%), >15 (23%). Note: nearly three-fourths have at least five years' professional experience; used to counter claims of inexperienced instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor teaching experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of prior academic teaching experience instructors possess (academic years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses: 0–2 yrs (7%), 3–5 (18%), 5–10 (32%), 10–15 (18%), >15 (25%). Three-quarters had at least five years teaching experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor academic rank and degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Current academic rank (instructor, assistant, associate, full professor) and highest earned degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data show many principal instructors hold senior ranks (associate/full) and advanced degrees (Ph.D., master's), although some hold bachelor's only. Caveat: results refer to principal instructor only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of teaching assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the principal instructor typically has assistance (other faculty, graduate TAs, undergraduate TAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76% answered 'no' to assistance, 24% 'yes'. Of those with assistance: 40% from other faculty, 43% graduate TAs, 17% undergraduate TAs. Conclusion: majority taught by principal instructor or assisted by faculty-level personnel; only ~14% involve TAs significantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of instructor's course load represented
rubrics_metrics.description: What proportion of the instructor’s total course load the basic course represents (e.g., 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses indicate some instructors devote 1/2 or more of load to the course (often when directing multi-section offerings). Used to understand faculty investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-academic professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether instructors use local/nearby press professionals as guest lecturers or interview subjects and how they are used/paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 57% use professionals, 43% do not. Usage: guest lecturers (49%), interview subjects (38%). In ~50% of cases professionals unpaid; ~20% are on payroll and often teach labs or sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecture/discussion time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of class hours per week typically allocated to lecture/discussion in the basic course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported: 1 hour (25%), 2 hours (50%), 3 hours (16%), 4 hours (5%), 5 hours (3%), >6 (1%). Indicates typical lecture time around 2 hours/week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of class hours per week typically allocated to laboratory sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported: 1 hr (7%), 2 hrs (31%), 3 hrs (26%), 4 hrs (24%), 5 hrs (6%), 6 hrs (3%), >6 (3%). Many programs include substantial lab time (2–4 hours common).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary texts used
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary or required textbook(s) used for the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 19 different primary texts listed. Most-favored: Interpretative Reporting (Curtis MacDougall) cited 27 times; Reporting (Mitchell Charnley) 24 times; others used no primary text (10 respondents). Choice of text varies widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary texts and reference materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary books and style guides used (e.g., AP-UPI Stylebook, Elements of Style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28 different supplemental texts cited; most frequently: AP-UPI Stylebook (38 mentions), The Elements of Style (17). Indicates reliance on style/reference materials for craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: news gathering techniques (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis placed on news gathering techniques in lectures/discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 responses: 'A great deal/Quite a lot' = 75%, 'Some' = 18%, 'Almost none' = 6%. Strongly emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: news writing techniques (story structure, transitions) (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on story structure and transitions in lecture/discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 95% 'A great deal/Quite a lot', 5% 'Some', 0% 'Almost none'. Very high priority topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: lead writing (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on lead writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 87% 'A great deal/Quite a lot', 11% 'Some', 2% 'Almost none'. Lead-writing is heavily stressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: news writing style (sentence length, readability, clarity) (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on writing style characteristics like clarity and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 93% 'A great deal/Quite a lot', 7% 'Some'. Style is a primary instructional focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: interviewing techniques (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on interviewing techniques in lecture/discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 64% 'A great deal/Quite a lot', 27% 'Some', 9% 'Almost none'. Interviewing commonly taught but less uniformly emphasized than leads/style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: history of journalism (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on journalism history during lecture/discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3% 'A great deal', 8% 'Some', 89% 'Almost none'. Most instructors do not emphasize history in this basic course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: legal hazards (libel, privacy) (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on legal hazards including libel and privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 19% 'A great deal', 52% 'Some', 29% 'Almost none'. Legal topics are covered to varying extents; may be taught in separate courses at some institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: diction (choice of words) (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on diction in lectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 60% 'A great deal', 30% 'Some', 10% 'Almost none'. Word choice is fairly emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: syntax (parallelism, placement of modifiers, sentence emphasis) (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on syntax-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 65% 'A great deal', 25% 'Some', 10% 'Almost none'. Syntactic craft is an important focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: spelling (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on spelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 66% 'A great deal', 24% 'Some', 10% 'Almost none'. Spelling is a common emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: news judgment (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on news judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 90% 'A great deal', 9% 'Some', 1% 'Almost none'. News judgment is almost universally emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: ethics (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on ethics in lectures/discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 53% 'A great deal', 32% 'Some', 15% 'Almost none'. Ethics often covered, though sometimes in separate courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: communication theory (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on communication theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 12% 'A great deal', 14% 'Some', 74% 'Almost none'. Usually not central in this basic course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: audience analysis (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on audience analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1% 'A great deal', 31% 'Some', 58% 'Almost none'. Rarely emphasized in basic course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: journalistic careers (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on careers in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10% 'A great deal', 31% 'Some', 59% 'Almost none'. Career topics are infrequently a major lecture topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis: current issues in reporting and newswriting (lecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on current issues (e.g., 'new journalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 21% 'A great deal', 56% 'Some', 23% 'Almost none'. Many instructors touch on current trends but not always in depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab writing situations: simulated standardized news situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of using standardized, simulated news situations set up in the lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3: 32% used them 'often', 25% 'more often', others less; use varies. Many instructors use simulated scenarios but not universally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab writing situations: actual on-campus events
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of assigning coverage of actual news events on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 25% 'often', 24% 'more often', 12% '1–3 times a term', 43% 'once a week' etc. On-campus events are a common lab source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab writing situations: actual off-campus events
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of assigning coverage of off-campus events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7% 'often', 15% 'more often', 12% '1–3 times a term', 38% 'once a week', 34% 'more than once a week'—varies widely across instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab writing situations: beat assignments on campus
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of assigning campus beat assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 23% 'often', 43% 'more often', 38% 'once a week', 78% 'more than once a week' for some—beat work on campus is widely used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab writing situations: beat assignments off campus
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of assigning off-campus beat assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 13% 'often', 7% 'more often', 34% 'once a week', 85% 'more than once a week' for some—off-campus beat coverage used but less frequently overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for setting up simulated news situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches used for simulated news situations (dittoed handouts, workbooks, instructor plays sources, TAs, student role-play, outside guests, audio/video tapes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most common: dittoed handouts (widely used); published workbooks declining; instructor simulates sources commonly used; teaching assistant simulations rare; students role-play and outside guests used; audio/video tapes and programmed instruction limited due to cost. Table 4 shows distribution by frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems emphasized in devised story situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Kinds of problems instructors design story situations to emphasize (assessing news values, accuracy, quotes, organization, libel avoidance, action sequences, balance, bias, taste, privacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranked counts: Assessing news values (85 mentions), Accuracy (82), Dealing with quotes (76), Organizing complex details (75), Avoidance of libel (59), Organizing action sequences (53), Balance (48), Avoidance of reporter bias (45), Problems of taste (41), Avoidance of invasion of privacy (15). Also interview techniques, attribution, clarity, conciseness, deadlines mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside writing situations used and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Types/frequency of outside assignments (meetings, speeches, student gov't, beat coverage, downtown government/speeches/meetings/beat coverage/interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 5 shows instructors rely heavily on on-campus meetings/speeches and campus beat coverage; downtown beat coverage used much less often. Many favor easily monitored on-campus events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical number of writing assignments per term
rubrics_metrics.description: How many writing assignments students complete during a typical term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses: <10 (3%), 10–19 (17%), 20–29 (36%), 30–39 (16%), 40+ (23%); a few reported up to 100. Many assignments are short, deadline-driven lab pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical assignment scope/duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether assignments are single-lab-period deadline pieces or multi-period investigative projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most assignments designed to be covered and written in one lab period (1–3 hours) under deadline, but many instructors include longer investigative assignments across lab periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing student copy: proportion edited/returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Of total assignments completed, how many are edited/corrected and handed back to students?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 6: 89% of assignments are edited/corrected and returned (i.e., virtually all student copy is processed rather than discarded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing student copy: who edits/corrects
rubrics_metrics.description: Of corrected/edited work, how much is corrected by the principal instructor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 80% of corrected work is handled by the principal instructor—significant instructor involvement in editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing student copy: assignments graded
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of assignments that receive a grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately half of assignments are graded (Table 6 shows variation); grading approaches vary (some use only final course grade).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing student copy: critiqued/discussed for class
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of assignments critiqued and discussed for the benefit of entire class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 28% (with variation) are critiqued for the whole class. Some instructors prefer private corrections, others general class discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of class critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques used when critiquing student copy for the class (reading aloud, transparencies, dittoed corrected stories, uncorrected handouts with class correction, open file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most favored: instructor reads copy aloud and notes corrections (69%); transparencies (41%); corrected ditto distribution (34%); uncorrected ditto with class correction (18%). Time and cost limit more efficient technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround time for feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: How soon edited and graded copy is returned to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before next class (10%), at next class (57%), within a week (28%), within two weeks (3%), at next scheduled individual conference (2%). Generally prompt feedback is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for communicating criticisms and suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Means by which instructors/TA communicate critiques (marginal comments, individual conferences, extensive written critiques, standardized checklist, computerized exercises).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marginal comments/editing on original copy (97%), individual conferences (81%), extensive written critiques (42%), standardized checklists (5%), computerized exercises (1%). Individual conferences are widely used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of individual conferences per student
rubrics_metrics.description: How many one-on-one conferences are scheduled per student during a term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among those using conferences: 1 (8%), 2 (34%), 3 (12%), 4 (6%), 5 (3%), 6 (5%), >6 (15%), varies (17%). Frequency varies; many students receive only a few brief conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of individual conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical time allocated to each individual conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10 minutes or less (10%), 10–15 minutes (36%), 15–30 minutes (34%), >30 minutes (4%), varies (17%). Guidance: effectiveness depends on quality as well as quantity of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for rewriting and publication of student copy
rubrics_metrics.description: How often student copy is returned for rewriting and how often student work is published (lab publication, campus newspaper/magazine, off-campus publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy returned to student to be rewritten: often/always (18%), sometimes (59%), seldom (12%), never (11%). Lab publication: 0% often, 9% sometimes, 6% seldom, 85% never. Campus publication and off-campus publication used to varying extents; report notes nearly a quarter seldom/never require rewrites—seen as surprising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading system used
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of grading scale employed (A–F, pass/fail, numerical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About 75% used traditional A–F; others used pass/fail or numerical scales. Choice of grading system varies but nearly all use some evaluative scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: recognition of news values
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which recognition of news values factors in grading student writing assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 95% 'A great deal/Quite a lot', 4% 'Some', 1% 'Almost none'. News values are central in grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: writing style (sentence length, clarity, readability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which writing style influences grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 100% 'A great deal/Quite a lot'. Writing style universally important in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which factual accuracy is weighted in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 100% 'A great deal/Quite a lot'. Accuracy is non-negotiable in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which spelling affects student grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 88% 'A great deal', 12% 'Some'. Spelling is strongly considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: diction (choice of words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which diction is considered in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 78% 'A great deal', 21% 'Some', 1% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: syntax (parallelism, placement of modifiers, sentence emphasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which syntax affects grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 78% 'A great deal', 21% 'Some', 1% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which transitions are emphasized in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 71% 'A great deal', 24% 'Some', 5% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of originality in grading student work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 62% 'A great deal', 26% 'Some', 12% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: lead devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which lead development is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 81% 'A great deal', 16% 'Some', 3% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: organization and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of organization and completeness in grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization: 94% 'A great deal'; Completeness: 92% 'A great deal'. These are core evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: fairness and handling of quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which fairness and correct handling of quotes factor in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness: 91% 'A great deal'; Handling of quotes: 88% 'A great deal'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in grading: avoidance of jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of jargon avoidance in grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 67% 'A great deal', 29% 'Some', 4% 'Almost none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination approaches for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of exams used to evaluate student achievement (standardized lab exercises, midterms, finals, spot quizzes, current events quizzes, take-home/field assignments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common methods include standardized lab exercises (45%), midterms (44%), finals (34%), spot quizzes (32%), current events quizzes (52%), and assignments requiring coverage away from lab (15%). Many instructors use multiple methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/lab enrollment size and accrediting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical lab section enrollment and accreditation concerns regarding practicability of large lab sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab section sizes reported: <15 students (19%), 15–20 (45%), 21–25 (14%), 26–30 (4%), 31–35 (2%), 36–40 (5%), >40 (11%). Accrediting teams usually criticize labs >15–20; yet 36% reported lab sections >20 students, indicating tension between standards and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common problems in teaching the course
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief problems instructors face: poorly motivated students, weak English/grammar, not enough time, too-large classes, lack of equipment, difficulty engaging students, mixed student levels, lack of assistance, non-majors slowing pace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 9 frequencies: Not enough time (37 mentions), Poorly-motivated/weak English (29), Too many students/classes too large (19), Lack of equipment (8), others fewer. These constraints inform quality judgments and improvement priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements to the course
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors' recommendations: more individual work, move away from contrived situations, adopt new techniques (programmed instruction), weed out misfits, get student work into print, reduce class size, emphasize doing over lecture, require more rewriting and field newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 counts: do more individual work (19 mentions), reduce contrived situations (16), adopt new techniques (9), weed out misfits (8), get more student work into print (8), cut class size (6), reduce lecture (6), require more rewriting (2). Several one-off suggestions: emphasize ethics/fairness, refresher training for teachers, clarify objectives, use workbooks, treat course as key professional course.
